newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev closes touch softer despite rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev closes touch softer despite rate rise.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 1,571-1,574 per dollar, flat on the opening's 1,571-1,575 but down from the midday's 1,570-1,572 as dollar bids from final clients stirred a dormant local market, traders said.
"A number of small final clients started bidding for foreign currency in the afternoon and sellers seized the opportunity to raise their ask prices for the dollar," a commercial bank dealer said.
News that the central bank would raise its main interest rate failed to boost demand for levs because it came shortly before the market closed.
Dealers said earlier on Thursday the Bulgarian National Bank had advised them it would raise its main interest rate to 48.72 percent annually from 43.08 percent, to take effect from Monday, June 2.
The new higher main rate could herald rising yields on floating interest T-bills and demand for this type of government securities could increase at Monday's auctions, traders said.
The Finance ministry has offered 20 billion lev worth of floating interest T-bills with maturities of six, nine and 12 months and no minimum acceptance price set in advance for the auctions.
Interest on each of the issues is set equal to the main interest rate until maturity and is adjusted every time the rate is changed.
